@dai9000 

Is there also an "Source IP Spoofing" output? Or was it just "Invalid packet" output? I wonder if there is a part where the UPF outputs on another line.

Do you think it would be good to upload a log file to share this part?

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

@dai9000 

In the uplink packet of the UE/gNB, the TEID and the UE's Source IP do not match. I can't figure out why the eNB is sending such a packet.

To make sure there are no other issues with Open5GS, we recommend that you share all log files from Open5GS.

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

If no one else is having problems, it's probably something on my end not compatible with something.

I'll probably try and go back to 2.4.7 as I know it was pretty stable on our system and didn't have the errors and lockups I've had with 2.4.10 or 2.4.11.

2.4.7 would sometimes run for weeks at a time without a problem. Since 2.4.10, it's never went more than 2 days without needing to be restarted.

@dai9000 

When v2.4.11 does not work properly, is it a situation in which a huge amount of logs are output to UPF such as IP Spoof? I'd just like to ask if there was any problem with the screen output.

Also, what is the situation in 2.4.7? Is the DROP log output by IP Spoof?

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

Up until 2.4.11 when something happened to lock up Open5gs server, it would at least segfault a process that I could setup an automated system to monitor in the log files and automatically restart the services.

Since 2.4.11, nothing segfaults or gives any indication of it not working, the log files just fill up with multiple Source IP-4 Spoofing and traffic just stops passing the the UEs.

2.4.7 would occasionally crash with a segfault, but it was pretty rare.

Right now I have a server with two Ethernet interfaces routing packets in from the Internet and out to the UEs and eNBs. I'm going to work on setting up a new server from scratch with a single 10Gbit fiber interface and see if it might act differently.

@dai9000 

Please share the test results when you get them. If you can share the open5gs log file, I'll know more.

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

In the last couple of days we just had the same "Source IP Spoofing" issue and UPF logs filling up. I have about 128MB of logs I can share with you, either let me know where you want me to send them or I can put them on Google Drive.

Our system only has one active customer and one test router currently and two active eNodeBs, plus a test eNodeB. Issues only started after upgrading to 2.4.11, I think we were on 2.4.7 previously.

Our server also uses  2 x Gigabit Ethernet ports.

@cmmacneill53 Please use the google drive.

It would also be helpful if you could explain what happened based on time.

Thanks a lot!
Sukchan

@acetcom 
I'll package up the logs later on and post a link, I'm a bit tied up with something else currently.

I reported in #1815 14 days ago issues with upgrading to 2.4.11 on Debian 10, but the only suggestion received was to remove and re-install the server. I haven't had a chance to do that yet. It's been working fine until the live customer reported no internet a few hours ago.

On reviewing the logs, upf.log suddenly started showing the "Source IP Spoofing" issue within 2 minutes (2022-10-17 02:57 NZDT) of our monitoring system losing connectivity with the customer router. It's taken the customer over 48 hours to report the issue. We don't proactively monitor connections, as many are on Solar Power, so are often turned off.

I attempted to resolve the problem by restarting only open5gs-mmed.service. DNS traffic then was passing to Google and CloudFlare, but strangely no other traffic. The customer router needed to be restarted to fully restore service. So not sure if it was the Router (Huawei B525-BA91) throwing a fit and taking down the EPC or vice versa.

Wish we had a way to go back to 2.4.7 or even 2.4.4. I know on our system with 2.4.7 we had less issues, and I have a virtual machine with 2.4.4 that seems great, but running our 180 or so customers, it couldn't handle the load and had throughput issues and loss of pings. I also tried setting up a virtual machine fresh with 2.4.11 and it couldn't support the load of 180 customers. (Does anyone know of any tweaks on VM machines that will help them run Open5gs reliably?)

Recently on our main system server running 2.4.11 on Ubuntu, after changing to a single Ethernet port for in and out and a few other tweaks, it has seemed better.

Since I've been switching between it and virtual servers to try, I've not ran Open5gs processes more than a couple of days between switchouts, so I've not had another instance of it not passing traffic to report yet.

I spoke too soon. It had been up about 48 hours and did that lockup again with log files flooding with IP Spoofing:
[DROP] Source IP-4 Spoofing APN:internet SrcIf:0 DstIf:1 TEID:0x8a
and some of these as well:
Invalid packet [IP version:6, Packet Length:116]

Is there any way to go back to 2.4.7 or even 2.4.4?

Guess I'm going to put a cron job to restart the Open4gs services every morning again.

@acetcom 

22.3MB TAR GZIPed error logs uploaded to https://drive.google.com/file/d/1m_-4hbfO8Ep-oWkxWvkHlogWIIMKMVDb/view?usp=sharing

File will be accessible for 24 hours, then I'll take it down.

TAR archive contains all logfiles for the last 4 days on our system.

Problem event commencted at 2022-10-17 02:57 NZDT

@dai9000

I originally evaluated Open5GS on a VM, but had no issues. We decided for production purposes we wanted to ring fence the loading and implemented on a dedicated server, but not a particularly fast one. It was a re-purposed 1U server with SoC processor and 2 x Gigabit Ethernet that had been used previously as a TV Streaming Server, continuously streaming several 100s of MBs of data with no issues.

We seem to have a limitation in our eNodeB and maximum capacity is 60Mbps per connection. With only one live customer and a couple of test connections, we haven't really put much load on our open5GS EPC, so not sure when or if we're going to hit some resource ceiling.

This doesn't really help your resource limitation issue, but I would certainly recommend dedicated hardware rather than a VM environment, especially for a live service. Unless you have full control of the Bare Metal HyperVisor, it's very easy for other VMs to be hogging resources that you don't have control over.

Yeah, we have a dedicated bare metal server currently, but wanted to put it on a dedicated VM in our control, just so it would be easier to roll back and have better control.

So, I've tried a dedicated VM running ProxMox and also trying XCP-ng on a dedicated VM server (with the same specs as our bare metal server), I experienced problems with latency and un-usability with Open5gs with 180 clients.

> Is ipv6 enabled in your environment？ Are these ipv6 addresses assigned to UE？

We aren't using ipv6 on any of our equipment. Don't know why that is showing up.

On reviewing my UPF logs again, I realised the SRC/UE addresses are IPv4 stated in Hex.

The SRC address is IMEI 999990000011 our live customer and UE is IMEI 999990000000003 which is our test router. So looks like something somewhere is getting confused over which UE econnection is which??????

The rest of the Hex in the UPF ERROR log seems to be a packet or header dump of some kind.

@myonlystarWang

The two routers I have currently connected (Huawei B525), support IPv6 but there are no specific settings in the Admin to change the behaviour or disable it. I found a post that someone responded to saying that the Huawei B525 only configures IPv6 on the WAN side if the APN supports it.

In the Open5GS database the Subscribers have an IPv6 address defined, but "Type" is set to IPv4 only, so this should have no effect. Maybe the code is ignoring the "Type" and attempting to setup IPv6 too?

I'll try removing the IPv6 addresses from the database, but if IPv6 is broken, it would be nice if this were fixed rather than just disabled.

Did you see my earlier comment that the Error message in the UPF logs seem to be confusing the two UE sessions:-

I do not see anything in my UPF logs that would imply any issue with IPv6, the error message explicity says IPv4 Spoofing.

10/17 02:57:20.221: [upf] ERROR: [DROP] Source IP-4 Spoofing APN:internet SrcIf:0 DstIf:1 TEID:0x9a (../src/upf/gtp-path.c:438)
10/17 02:57:20.221: [upf] ERROR:        SRC:67CCF80B, UE:67CCF803 (../src/upf/gtp-path.c:440)

SRC:67CCF80B translates to the IPv4 addr 103.204.248.11 which is my live customer.

UE:67CCF803  translates to the IPv4 addr 103.204.248.3 which is the test router.

As the error message isn't very verbose, it's difficult to guess what information it's trying to convey. I guess it's trying to highlight that the system received a packet with source IP 103.204.248.11, but was expecting the source IP to be 103.204.248.3???

Can anyone explain what the error message actually means, then we may have a chance of working out what's causing it.

@cmmacneill53 

From your log file, SGW-C received "Context Not Found" in Delete-Session-Response. SMF seems to have restarted. Source IP spoofing doesn't seem to be an issue with your network environment. This is because SMF is restarted and TEID mismatch between sgwu and upf.

It would be of great help if you could compile the sources and capture those logs with gdb as below.

```
$ git clone https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs
$ cd open5gs
$ meson build --prefix=`pwd`/install
$ cd build
$ ninja install
$ cd ..
```

And then run smf using gdb.
```
$ gdb ./install/bin/open5gs-smfd
(if crashed, we can see the backtrace in gdb shell)
> bt
```

Thank you so much for sharing this.
Sukchan

The router with ip 103.204.248.3 is the real UE which had the modem connected to open5gs  and the customer with ip 103.204.248.11 is the PC which connected to the LAN port of the router?
If so ,it make sense

@myonlystarWang

The IP addresses are for two distinct Routers at physically different locations with unique SIM cards. All LAN side devices connected to these routers are NATed, so there should never be more than one public IP per Router.

@cmmacneill53 

I missed one thing: using the v2.4.11 tag is better.

- Git clone
```
$ git clone https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs
$ cd open5gs
```

- Change v2.4.11 tag
```
$ git checkout v2.4.11
```

- Build Open5GS
```
$ meson build --prefix=`pwd`/install
$ cd build
$ ninja install
$ cd ..
```

In this case, other NFs can use the package as-is. You only need to run SMF with gdb.

- Stop SMF in the package
```
$ sudo systemctl stop open5gs-smfd
```

- And then run SMF using gdb.
```
$ gdb ./install/bin/open5gs-smfd
(if crashed, we can see the backtrace in gdb shell)
> bt
```

Thank you so much!
Sukchan

OK，If so, you should follow acetcom‘s advices to get log，that will be more helpful

@cmmacneill53 

I looked carefully at your logs, and SMF doesn't seem to crash. And there is no log of normal shutdown and restart of SMF based on the log you shared.

If so, it is very likely that SMF has a bug.

I don't think it's necessary to compile the source code and look at the gdb log. Even though this often happens during troubleshooting, I'm really sorry for misguided.

I  wish this was reproducible in your environment. If so, turn it on at the debug level of MME, SGW-C, SMF, PCRF, and HSS. SGW-U and UPF don't need to do that.

You can turn on debug of MME like below.
```diff
$ diff --git a/configs/open5gs/mme.yaml.in b/configs/open5gs/mme.yaml.in
index 384d8f885..1c48c730b 100644
--- a/configs/open5gs/mme.yaml.in
+++ b/configs/open5gs/mme.yaml.in
@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@
 #
 logger:
     file: @localstatedir@/log/open5gs/mme.log
+    level: debug
 
 #
 # mme:
```

Likewise, please turn on debug log by modifying the configuration files of the remaining SGW-C, SMF, PCRF, and HSS.

You probably only have a small number of UEs in your environment. Therefore, it is recommended that you share wireshark logs if possible. Using the filter below you can only capture the control plane.
```
s1ap || gtpv2 || pfcp || diameter
```

The wireshark log is not required, but it can tell us more information that the open5gs log doesn't know.

Thank you so much!
Sukchan

@cmmacneill53 and @dai9000 

There was a problem in v2.4.11 that the SGW-U Session was not properly deleted. v2.4.4 did not have this problem. So, I've fixed and release it in v2.5.0 soon.

For your reference, new NF(SCP) was added in v2.5.0. It's ok to use the settings as they are, but if you change the settings to a new one, you need to consider the SCP.

Please let me know if you have test results.

Thanks a lot!
